front.title: Policy Provision and Governance Inheritance from an Organisational Identity Substrate

abstract.t: An agent runtime that acts under an organisation's rules receives those rules in a form specific to each deployment, and the audit records it sends back are specific to each deployment too. This memo specifies two elements that two implementations would have to agree on. The first is an enforcement-gate specification, a list of rules, each with a trigger predicate over a tool invocation's name and arguments, an action (block, prompt for confirmation, or allow with audit), an applicability scope and an explanation, with the most restrictive action prevailing when several rules match. The second is an audit-signal record that the runtime submits to an append-only ingestion endpoint. Both are exposed as typed Model Context Protocol surfaces of an organisational identity substrate. The runtime resolves the substrate at session start from a manifest source. A principal bound to more than one substrate operates under the strictest applicable gate, and no substrate learns of another. The memo is Informational. The only implementation is the author's own substrate, and no agent runtime yet fetches policy this way.
